content.comment_body: Hello, I am experiencing difficulty connecting to a [product_name] module. I've noticed a symbol on the screen, which is shown in the attached image. Can someone clarify what this signal indicates? It appears in a 1 second on/off cycle. Is it possible that this symbol is causing the connection issue? Thank you in advance.

What are the IP and subnet settings for both the module and your PC? How is your network structured? Can you ping the module? If you're using [product_name] software to access it, have you selected the correct network card? I haven't seen this symbol on the module before, and I don't have a recent [version_no] available to test. However, this likely isn't related to your connection issue. Greetings, [user_name]
[product_name] settings: IP: 169.254.128.1 Subnet: 255.255.0.0 Gateway: 169.254.0.0 PC settings: IP: 169.254.128.124 Subnet: 255.255.0.0 Gateway: (not set) I am able to ping the [product_name].

@[user_name], My [product_name] display also shows this symbol, but I am not certain of its function. I've seen it in message notifications and menu screens, and I can connect my PC to the module without issue.

From what I recall, this symbol has appeared in the [version_no] series since its launch. It's a useful feature for support staff to demonstrate commitment. However, the documentation does not seem to explain this symbol. There are other unexplained symbols on the top right of the [product_name] operator device as well.
I've found a solution: I was using [product_name] software version [version_no], and after upgrading to [version_no] I was able to communicate with the module.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encountered connectivity problems with a [product_name] module, initially suspecting that an ambiguous symbol on the display was responsible. The core issue turned out to be software version incompatibility—updating from an older to a newer [product_name] software version resolved the problem. Additionally, users noted that documentation lacked information about certain display symbols, adding confusion during troubleshooting.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect reliable communication between [product_name] software and hardware modules, as well as clear documentation and display indicators to help interpret status symbols.
